title: Implicit surface
text:
There are various algorithms for rendering implicit surfaces,[1] including the marching cubes algorithm.[2] Essentially there are two ideas for visualizing an implicit surface: One generates a net of polygons which is visualized (see surface triangulation) and the second relies on ray tracing which determines intersection points of rays with the surface.[3] The intersection points can be approximated by sphere tracing, using a signed distance function to find the distance to the surface.[4]

### Implicit surface software

### Free implicit surface software

Open-source or free software supporting algebraic implicit surface modelling:

K3DSurf — A program to visualize and manipulate Mathematical models in 3-6 dimensions. K3DSurf supports Parametric equations and Isosurfaces

CGAL (Computational Geometry Algorithms Library), written in C++, has strong support for implicit surface modeling (Boolean operations on implicit surfaces, Surface meshing for visualization, Implicit curve arrangements).

PyVista[5], a Python wrapper around VTK for easier handling of implicit surfaces. Simplified API for rendering and manipulating implicit surfaces. It can integrate with numpy.

Some Blender add-ons (metaballs and volumetric modeling for implicit surfaces, and scripting support for custom implicit functions).

SculptsFEM (for solving PDEs on implicit surfaces, Implicit curve generation)

ImpliSolid[6] (open-source), supports sharp edges.

Houdini (supports implicit surface modeling using SDFs and procedural techniques). Houdini Apprentice License is free.[7]

POV-Ray (Persistence of Vision Raytracer) has built-in support for defining complex implicit surfaces.[8]

Vision-based surface reconstruction use implicit functions for statistical modelling of surfaces: SDFStudio,[9] Geo-Neus,[10] PointSDF,[11] etc.

Various other software exist for polygonization of implicit surfaces, in context of Marching cubes, and in general Image-based meshing and, but they are not necessarily based on an algebraic closed-form field.

### Industrial or commercial software using implicit surface software

Altair Inspire[12,13]

Leapfrog, implicit geological modelling software by Seequent, widely used in mining and environmental applications.

Studio RM, geologic modelling software by Datamine Software, supports implicit surface generation for mineral resource estimation.

K-MINE, mining and geological modelling software that uses implicit surfaces for orebody modelling.

Maple has a library for plotting implicit surfaces.
